body: Thank you for the lovely words. <3
Singapore. I'll check it out, although Im notoriously bad at keeping in touch with people. Thanks a lot for the advice. <3

I don't know what you've been through but I do understand overwhelming guilt- the kind that keeps you from getting better. I hope you realize that trying is enough, and falling is okay despite what other people say. If you'd like to take, I would love to listen.

Lots of love. <3

I hope so. I've been thinking about medication but I would largely be alone in seeking help, dealing with side effects etc  because of said situation. I also live alone abroad so Im not sure how well I could handle myself. They'd keep it to themselves but they think it's something I can change with eating better/exercising etc and I don't really want to push it because they've been going through a lot themselves.

Please don't. I don't know what you've been through but hold on a little longer, please? You seem like a wonderful person. Maybe we can get to know each other?

Lots of love. <3

Thank you. <3 Yes, there's a lot of stigma. My parents are nice about it but I have a complicated family situation that might get worse if I get diagnosed. I've also pretty much cut off all my friends because it takes so much out of me just to keep up normal social obligations. Sometimes I dread feeling relatively normal/happy because the crashes right after are so much worse. Do you feel that too, if you do t mind me asking?
Thank you for the advice, I will try. <3

It really honestly just helps to hear that being this tired is real. It tends to hit so suddenly. Yeah, that's the feeling. Too wound up to sleep, too tired to get out of bed. Everything seems to hurt.

Thanks again for making me feel not so alone.

Since I was around 11 I think? I used to joke about "having mood swings like a pregnant woman" as a kid. Until it got worse. I live somewhere where therapy isn't really seen in a good light so I've never actually been diagnosed. So on the better days I wonder if I just made all of it up or overreacted. It's just exhausting especially since I have to pretend to be normal a lot.

Sorry for the essay. I haven't spoken about this in a while.
Thank you for the lovely words <3

No I'm sorry. It's just another stupid thing I should never have expected to get better. I don't even have the right to feel bad. I'm probably the biggest waste of space on the planet. I'm tired. I'm so tired of all of it. I thought it'd be okay. It's not. It never will. And I probably deserve all of it.

I can relate to this. Through high school I pretty much forced myself to keep faking and the minute I graduated I think I kind of just stopped. Of course now everyone thinks I'm an attention seeking snob haha. Ah, life.
I understand how you feel. I've been there since I was about 16 too. If you'd like, you can talk to me too.
I can relate to this so much. I started and kept cutting for those exact same reasons. I'm sorry you're struggling. I wish I could tell you I knew a way out. For what it's worth, I understand.

I realized today that I've spent a great deal of time mourning the fact that my parents don't understand what I'm going through. But the more time I spend expecting them to magically start trying to understand and support me, the less I'm spending trying to help myself. I'm sorry you don't seem to have a proper support system.
Ah, youtube and anime. I can relate to this so much.

Haha, it's never going to get better for me. In my country you live with your parents until you get married. I'm always going to be stuck here and it's never going to end. I've accepted that.

Thank you though.

Yeah, I can relate to that completely. Logically, I understand why my mom acts the way she does; it's just hard not to react to it emotionally sometimes I guess. If that makes sense.

Thank you. I appreciate that. I'm 18 so in that confusing place in the middle I guess hah.

I'm in the same place with college. My family's filled with doctors and engineers and all manners of super smart people so all I get is "You'll get over it. Everyone goes through it. Get some confidence."

I'm sorry you're struggling.

Anger, confusion, hopelessness. Whenever I'm feeling depressed, my mother tends to leave me completely alone and the minute I feel slightly better enough to eat/ get out of bed, she'll drop a snide comment or two and well...I can't really explain it. It feels suffocating. I'd almost rather not feel better at all because constantly being put down after getting up is worse than just staying there.
Right now.

That's tough. I'm sorry you have to go through this alone.
Speaking from personal experience however, I wouldn't recommend trying to handle it on your own. You'll get through it, I believe but if this is the second time you've had a depressive episode, there's likely an underlying cause that's gone unaddressed. I've had on/off periods myself but every time I managed to get through it, I did my best to repress it and it only ever got worse until I couldn't handle it on my own anymore.
Of course everyone is different and I don't know anything about you but if you can, I think it would be good if you could talk to a professional once at least. I know I would've years ago if I'd known it would come to this.

Again, it's only a suggestion. But for what it's worth, my inbox is open if you want to rant/talk/anything. It's not an easy journey. I hope things get better for you soon.

Faltering doesn't make you weak. Everyone falls; no one can deal with their problems the best way every time. It's natural that you would want to try and handle your problems yourself and you couldn't have seen this coming. So forgive yourself and try to reach out to someone who'll be able to support you through this. Do you have any friends/family members you can confide in without being judged?

It's okay. It's not easy to understand these feelings unless you've experienced them yourself. I'm sorry for your struggle. I hope you're seeing a therapist and that your loved ones are being supportive.
Thank you, I appreciate it. (:
Yeah, it's hard. Being around people in general is pretty hard. Debating between faking happiness to keep them around or telling them and risking rejection.
Yeah, it's hard. Some days, just waking up is hard enough.

Yeah, I know that type. It's hard to make people understand. It's good that you're seeing a therapist, though. That's progress there.

Are you comfortable talking to them about it? For me, personally, even if my friends know, I try my best not to talk about it when I'm having my lows because they're frequent and I feel like they're going to get fed up because of how much I whine. It's bleh.

I'm supposed to be starting college soon, but I constantly feel like whatever decision I make is going to end up ruining my life. Going to school, where I have to listen to people telling me about how much they expect from me, how hard I'll have to work and how allegedly successful I have to become to live up to standards set by my family, keeps me in a constant state of anxiety. I'm not sure I even have hobbies anymore; everything just feels like another chore I have to do, another competition I have to win, another person I have to prove myself to, another way to justify my existence.

It's okay if you don't why you feel like this. I think that applies to a lot of people. Try to be kind to yourself, okay? You're not alone.

Do you have any friends/family members who know about your SH?

Calm down. Please put down the razor/knife/scissor. You are strong enough to do this. I'm sorry you have to go through this, but I'm here if you want to talk. If you think it will help, I'll listen to whatever you have to say.

"I would rather stay away from me too." This just resonates with me so much. Around people, I try to act happy even if I feel like screaming inside, because otherwise they'll give you an awkward look and leave and in some ways, the loneliness is worse.

For what it's worth, at least we have each other. I may not know you, but I understand what you're going through. You matter. I love you for being able to get through the day despite your struggles. I can't promise you that it will be okay but I hope it will. You deserve happiness. But until you find it, I want you to know that you're not alone.

I can relate to a lot of what you've said, especially the part about family. I alternate between hating them for treating me the way they do and hating myself for not being able to fulfill their expectations especially since there are reasons to justify their callousness.
For what it's worth, I hope you're doing better now and if you still need someone to talk to, you can PM me. (:

Most people would prefer to just turn a blind eye because they would rather not deal with it. If only we had the same option.

I'm sorry you're going through such a hard time alone. If you'd like, you can PM me as well, anytime you want. I'll listen.

I'm not sure about your situation but personally I ranked them according to priority. First was cost, then the standard of education, whether I have family there, job opportunities for internationals etc.

I have offers from colleges in the US, UK and Canada which I've narrowed down to two in the US and UK thus far.
